subject: English L1
title: Unit 4: Past Simple and Time Clauses

A.q: When I _____ ten years old, I _____ tennis.
A.explain: 'I' takes was, and played is simple past. Were is used with you and plural subjects, and play is present.

A.q: My grandparents always _____ fresh bread at home when I was little.
A.explain: Had is simple past, and the phrase 'when I was little' marks the past. Have is present plural, has is present singular, and having is a participle.

A.q: My parents and I _____ at the airport very early yesterday morning.
A.explain: The plural subject needs were, and the phrase 'yesterday morning' marks the past. Was is singular, are is present, and been needs a helping verb.

A.q: The glass _____ when it hit the floor.
A.explain: Broke is simple past. Break is present, broken is a participle, and breaking is continuous.

A.q: During the last mission, the astronauts _____ their pens float in microgravity.
A.explain: Watched is simple past, and the phrase 'during the last mission' marks the past. Watch is present, watching is continuous, and watches is third-person present.

A.q: When the principal _____ to the hall, the students stopped talking.
A.explain: Came is simple past in the time clause. Come is present, comes is third-person present, and coming is continuous.

A.q: The audience _____ upset when the singer canceled the show.
A.explain: Got is simple past. Get is present, gets is third-person present, and getting is continuous.

A.q: We _____ when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
A.explain: Screamed is simple past. Scream is present, screaming is continuous, and screams is third-person present.

A.q: I _____ on the report all morning before my manager called.
A.explain: Worked is simple past. Work is present, working is continuous, and works is third-person present.

A.q: The chef _____ the soup before the restaurant opened.
A.explain: Cooked is simple past. Cook is present, cooking is continuous, and cooks is third-person present.

A.q: When the crew _____ a leak in the oxygen tank, they began repairs.
A.explain: Detected is simple past. Detect is present, detecting is continuous, and detects is third-person present.

A.q: Which sentence is correct?

options: When did you start working at the clinic?
When you started working at the clinic?
When did you started working at the clinic?
When you start working at the clinic?
Did you finish your homework last night?
Did you finished your homework last night?
Did you finishes your homework last night?
Did you finishing your homework last night?
The nurse checked my temperature yesterday.
The nurse check my temperature yesterday.
The nurse checks my temperature yesterday.
The nurse checking my temperature yesterday.
Last year our class took a trip to the museum.
Last year our class take a trip to the museum.
Last year our class takes a trip to the museum.
Last year our class taking a trip to the museum.
The clinic opened a new waiting room last month.
The clinic open a new waiting room last month.
The clinic opens a new waiting room last month.
The clinic opening a new waiting room last month.
We didn't need a referral for the blood test last month.
We don't needed a referral for the blood test last month.
We didn't needed a referral for the blood test last month.
We don't need a referral for the blood test last month.
The patient didn't go to the clinic after the checkup.
The patient didn't went to the clinic after the checkup.
The patient don't go to the clinic after the checkup.
The patient wasn't go to the clinic after the checkup.
We weren't surprised when the results came out.
We wasn't surprised when the results came out.
We aren't surprised when the results came out.
We didn't surprised when the results came out.

A.explain: Steps 1-2 use did + the base verb in past questions. Steps 3-5 use simple past verbs in affirmative statements, and steps 6-7 use didn't + the base verb. Step 8 uses weren't with the plural subject 'we'.

A.q: Which sentence is correct?

options: They left the house when the rain stopped.
They leave the house when the rain stopped.
They left the house when the rain stop.
They leaving the house when the rain stopped.
The astronauts were in microgravity for six months.
The astronauts was in microgravity for six months.
The astronauts are in microgravity for six months.
The astronauts been in microgravity for six months.
She locked the door before she left the office.
She lock the door before she left the office.
She locked the door before she leave the office.
She locking the door before she left the office.
Did you enjoy the film last night?
Did you enjoyed the film last night?
Do you enjoy the film last night?
Did you enjoying the film last night?
The ships weren't ready when the storm arrived.
The ships wasn't ready when the storm arrived.
The ships aren't ready when the storm arrived.
The ships didn't ready when the storm arrived.
We shouted when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
We shout when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
We shouting when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
We shouts when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
The shop opened a new section last month.
The shop open a new section last month.
The shop opens a new section last month.
The shop opening a new section last month.
I called my brother after I finished my homework.
I call my brother after I finished my homework.
I calling my brother after I finished my homework.
I calls my brother after I finished my homework.
Yesterday the receptionist answered forty phone calls.
Yesterday the receptionist answer forty phone calls.
Yesterday the receptionist answers forty phone calls.
Yesterday the receptionist answering forty phone calls.

A.explain: Steps 1, 3, 7, 9, and 10 use simple past verbs in sentences with when, before, and after. Steps 2 and 6 use were or weren't with plural subjects, and steps 4-5 use did or didn't + the base verb. Step 11 uses were in a plural past question about 'your cousins'.

A.q: Last night, ___ a serious fire in the old market.
A.explain: The singular noun phrase 'a serious fire' takes there was. There were is plural, was there is question order, and were there is plural question order.

A.q: ___ many visitors at the museum?
A.explain: Were there is correct for a plural question about visitors. There were is statement order, was there is singular, and there was is singular statement order.

A.q: Were there many visitors at the museum? Yes, ___.
A.explain: There were is the correct plural short answer. There was is singular, and the options with 'they' change the subject.

A.q: My cousins ___ at my flat last weekend.
A.explain: The plural subject 'my cousins' and the phrase 'last weekend' require were all. Was all is singular, are all is present, and been all needs a helping verb.

A.q: I ___ time to call you yesterday.
A.explain: Didn't have is the correct past negative. Don't have is present, haven't had is present perfect, and didn't had is a double past error.

A.q: What ___ he ___ at the meeting yesterday?
A.explain: Did / say is correct because did + subject + base verb forms a past question. Do / say is present, did / said is a double past error, and are / saying is present continuous.

A.q: The campfire burned ___ sunrise.
A.explain: Until marks the endpoint of the continued burning. While needs a clause with another ongoing action, as soon as marks an immediate point, and since marks a start.

A.q: When I ___ a poor mark on the test, I decided to study harder.
A.explain: Got is simple past. Get is present, getting is continuous, and was get is not a valid past form.

A.q: Alexander Fleming ___ penicillin in 1928.
A.explain: Discovered is simple past for a single event. Discovers is present, discovering is a participle, and 'used to' describes past habits, not a single event.

A.q: The reaction _____ when the two chemicals were mixed.
A.explain: Began is simple past. Begin is present, begun is a participle, and beginning is continuous.
